solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Huge performance by one of two presenters in charge

parts.note: a gig is a musical performance
Ant is one half of Ant and Dec, the British TV presenting duo

explanation.surface: A TV presenter puts on an enormous show.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a famous British TV presenting double act; ANT is one of the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something gigantic is enormous in size.

clue.text: Part of building's framework making one smile

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
to beam is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: Something in a building's structure is cheerful enough to raise a grin.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel girder with an I-shaped cross-section, used in structural frames.

clue.text: Change about to be introduced making for quarrel

indicators.note: the short word for about is introduced into the word for change, so it goes inside

parts.note: an alteration is a change
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A change about to come in leads to an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be introduced' puts C (circa) inside ALTERATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an altercation is a noisy dispute or argument.

clue.text: Sonnet is about strained relationships

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of sonnet is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poem is written on the subject of difficult relationships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals the anagram of SONNET IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tensions are strained feelings or relations between people.

clue.text: Selfish tetrarch, awful ruler coming to bad end

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of selfish tetrarch are in a terrible mess, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A selfish petty ruler, an awful king, meets a sticky end.
explanation.walkthrough: A tetrarch ruled a quarter of a province; the surface fits the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: English king beheaded in 1649 after the Civil War, a monarch whose reign ended badly.

clue.text: Attractive features of cleaner, modern miss

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady, short for charwoman
Ms is the modern title used instead of Miss

explanation.surface: A cleaner and a young modern woman both have appealing qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is an old British term for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: charms are pleasing qualities that attract people.

clue.text: Minister had to trail after dog

indicators.note: to trail after means to follow behind, so this piece comes after the dog

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to have a meal is to eat it, so had gives ate

explanation.surface: A clergyman had to follow a dog around.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant clergyman, a minister of the church.

clue.text: Notice nothing that would create fuss

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An empty notice would cause a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ado is bother or fuss, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: The little guy's defence system

parts.note: minute means very small, little
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: The small man has his own protective arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuteman is a US intercontinental ballistic missile, part of America's nuclear deterrent.

clue.text: College blokes penning awful rot

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the men hold the other letters inside

parts.note: blokes are men

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of rot are in a mess and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Fellows at a college are writing dreadful nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' reads as writing and 'awful' as a verdict on the prose, but they are the containment and anagram signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Merton is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Brought to life, submerged in river or up in the sky?

indicators.note: submerged in means placed under water inside the river, so it goes inside

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England
a child brought to life is born

explanation.surface: Something born in a river, or up above it in the air?
explanation.walkthrough: The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airborne is flying, carried up in the air.

clue.text: Order given by a king or caliph

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A decree from a king or a caliph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' seems a command; here it is the Order of Merit, OM.
explanation.definitionFit: Omar was the second Muslim caliph, a successor to Muhammad.

clue.text: I will repeat for one with language difficulties

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: Someone struggling with language says they will keep repeating things.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun use: an illiterate is a person unable to read or write.

clue.text: Lessons about faith and prayer boy remembered

parts.note: RE is religious education, school lessons about religion
a collect is a short prayer in the liturgy
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy recalls his lessons on religion and prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is a British school subject; a collect is a short church prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have recollected something is to have recalled it.

clue.text: Geographical features — some collapsing with infiltration of water

indicators.note: infiltration means getting inside, so the water goes into the rearranged letters
collapsing suggests the word some falls apart and is rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Landforms, some of them collapsing as water seeps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' (anagram) and 'with infiltration of' (containment) blend into a picture of erosion, hiding their roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Moraines are ridges of rock debris deposited by glaciers, landforms studied in geography.

clue.text: Maiden possibly about to perform and go over the top?

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs, so a maiden is one kind of over
re means about or concerning
to act is to perform

explanation.surface: A young woman about to perform might get carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a maiden is an over of six balls from which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to go over the top is to respond too strongly.

clue.text: Theatrical Conservative, a person in the House

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, sitting in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A flamboyant Tory, one of the members of the House.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: camp behaviour is exaggerated and showy.

clue.text: Symbolic item brought out in Latin Mass mostly

indicators.note: brought out suggests the letters are worked out into a new shape, so they are rearranged
mostly means all but the last letter of the word mass is kept

explanation.surface: A sacred object is produced during a Latin Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final S of MASS; 'brought out' rearranges LATIN + MAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is a charm or object thought to have magical or protective power.

clue.text: Priest in little village

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words little village

explanation.surface: A clergyman lives in a small village.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Levi was the founder of the priestly tribe of Israel; a Levite served as priest.

clue.text: Policy by principal is newspaper feature

indicators.note: by means next to, so the policy word sits beside the principal's

parts.note: a head is a school principal
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A school head's policy makes the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline is the title printed in large type above a newspaper story.

clue.text: Warriors quiet and wicked

parts.note: an impi is a regiment of Zulu warriors
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Fighters who are both silent and evil.
explanation.walkthrough: An impi is a body of Zulu warriors, a regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischievous sense: wicked can mean playfully naughty, like a little imp.

clue.text: Great legal expert could give grunt if mad

indicators.note: could give says the letters of grunt if mad can be rearranged to produce the result

explanation.surface: An eminent lawyer might grunt when angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder GRUNT IF MAD; 'could give' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand mufti is the senior expert in Islamic law in a country.

clue.text: What's the point of big meal without a starter?

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so the first letter of the meal word is dropped

parts.note: a feast is a big meal

explanation.surface: Why have a big dinner without a first course?
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's the point' reads as a question of purpose; it defines a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Rob gets wages

definitions.meaning: to swindle or extort money from someone

explanation.surface: A thief takes away people's pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang twice: to cheat someone out of money, and a person's weekly pay.

clue.text: Less consistent Greek character embraced by father

indicators.note: being embraced by means held inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: pater is Latin for father, used in old-fashioned British slang
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man hugged by his dad is acting inconsistently.
explanation.definitionFit: Something patchier is more uneven or irregular in quality.

clue.text: Vineyard gang reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word for gang is heard rather than written

parts.note: a crew is a gang

explanation.surface: A band of workers in a vineyard is the talk of the town.
explanation.definitionFit: French wine term: a cru is a vineyard or its classified growth.

clue.text: Victor behaving like an adult?

definitions.meaning: the first name of Victor ..., Hollywood actor of the 1940s and 1950s
acting in a grown-up, sensible way

explanation.surface: A winner shows grown-up behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' reads as a winner; it is the actor Victor Mature, star of Samson and Delilah.
explanation.definitionFit: Surname of the actor Victor, and an adjective for grown-up, sensible conduct.

clue.text: Canonised OT woman? Gosh!

parts.note: a canonised person is a saint, abbreviated St
Ruth is a woman in the Old Testament, with a book named after her

explanation.surface: Was the Old Testament woman made a saint? Good heavens!
explanation.walkthrough: Struth (God's truth) is a British and Australian exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise or dismay.

clue.text: Dull, like a very flat note?

definitions.meaning: to dull is to soften or moderate something
a note so flat its pitch has dropped, read as a musical tone that is down

explanation.surface: A flat musical note sounds lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: To tone down is to moderate or soften; literally, a tone lowered in pitch.
